Added 10 new integration tests to mcp-server/tests/gui/project-detail-runs.test.ts across three new describe blocks: (1) WP-005 Inline edit survives data-only poll ticks — title edit input value preserved, slug edit input value preserved, multiple sequential poll ticks don't destroy active edit; (2) WP-005 Single-interval invariant — combined poll registers once, startResumePolling replaces combined interval with single 3s call, two sequential renders each register exactly one poll, _clearPolling called on structural stopPolling; (3) WP-005 Modal and archive/unarchive remain functional — reset button present under polling, DOM patching skipped when modal open, archive banner renders for ARCHIVED project.

comments.note: The makeProject() helper in project-detail-auto-update.test.ts and project-detail-runs.test.ts have slightly different structures for handling overrides (_metaOverrides, _rootOverrides patterns differ). A shared test-helpers module for the project-detail test suite would reduce this divergence and make it easier to maintain consistent project fixtures across the 5+ test files that share this pattern.

The 'title edit input preserves focus state' aspect of AC-5 is tested implicitly (the input element remains mounted), but jsdom does not implement the :focus pseudoclass or document.activeElement reliably enough to assert focus directly. The tests verify the stronger property — that the input element itself survives poll ticks unmounted — which is the underlying mechanism that preserves focus. A real browser E2E test would be needed to assert actual focus state.

The resume-triggered handoff test (single-interval invariant, combined→resume) relies on the Resume button appearing in the DOM within 300ms. In CI environments with high load this flush loop may need a longer deadline. The existing project-detail-runs.test.ts tests use the same 300ms pattern, so this is consistent with the established convention.

comments.note: makeProject() in project-detail-auto-update.test.ts (line 129) unconditionally spreads `...overrides` into `meta`, which causes leakage of top-level sentinel keys (_metaOverrides, _rootOverrides, work_packages, synthesis_generated) into the meta object. Verified via Node: '_metaOverrides' and 'synthesis_generated' appear as meta keys when those overrides are provided. No current test breaks because project-detail.js reads specific known keys from meta and ignores extras — but this could mislead future test authors who read the API shape from the test fixture. The `_metaOverrides`/`_rootOverrides` escape-hatch pattern also goes unused by any current test. Not Blocking (all tests pass and the runtime behavior is correct), but worth addressing in a follow-up by cleaning up the helper to not spread the full overrides bag into meta.

[documentation-forward] The jsdom limitation on document.activeElement / :focus pseudoclass (why focus state is tested via element survival rather than direct assertion) is documented in Developer pipeline comments but not in the test file itself. A brief comment above the 'title edit input value is preserved' tests in both files explaining this testing strategy would help future contributors understand why the test doesn't call document.activeElement directly.

[documentation-forward] The makeProject() helpers diverge between project-detail-auto-update.test.ts (uses _metaOverrides/_rootOverrides sentinel keys) and project-detail-runs.test.ts (flat spread into meta). The README.md for the GUI test suite (mcp-server/tests/gui/README.md) does not document the fixture helper pattern. Adding a note about the intended makeProject() shape and the divergence risk would help contributors working across both files.

In project-detail-runs.test.ts, the global beforeEach installs mock implementations first (lines 55–64) then calls vi.clearAllMocks() (line 65), which resets them immediately. This is a pre-existing pattern (not introduced by WP-005) and doesn't cause failures because renderWithAPI re-stubs per-call. However, project-detail-auto-update.test.ts correctly reverses this order (clearAllMocks first, then re-install). The inconsistency is cosmetic but could confuse future contributors if they rely on the global beforeEach mocks being active.
